verdicts.note: 'Serve the people, not the bureaucracy' and 'responsible stewardship of taxpayer dollars' [S4], repeated in the primary statement [S1] and the general statement ('efficient, accountable' government, 'long-term stewardship of taxpayer dollars') [S8]. These are his own words, not an endorsement inference. No specific cuts, so -1 at medium.

Outsider framing ('not running to become a career politician' [S8]) against an institutional profile: Planning Commission chair confirmed by the council [S2], elected Charter Review commissioner [S3], several county advisory boards [S4]. Genuinely mixed, so 0 at medium. Minor: the scoring highlight 'elected 2026 Charter Review commissioner' should read 2025-2026 (the dossier says he served on the 2025-2026 commission; Barrans' dossier says the election was in 2025).

S4 is her own signed answers to the 31st LD Democrats questionnaire (checked in the cached copy: 'Yes' to 'tax reform and progressive taxes as wealth increases' and 'Yes' to raising developer impact fees). The questionnaire went to a Democratic group, but the score rests on her stated answers, not on party or the endorsement. Yes/no answers to the asker's wording support medium, not high.

Her free-text answers ask for more infrastructure money for unincorporated areas, new bus service to Orting, Buckley and Graham, more funding for rural mobile outreach and for unhoused college students [S4][S6]; her statement adds affordable housing, access to care and rural infrastructure as priorities [S10]. Consistent toward investment; +1 medium.

'Yes' to robust investment in public or subsidized housing, plus rent subsidies [S4], and affordable housing as a statement priority [S10]; density and accessory-unit incentives [S6] pull toward supply, so +1 not +2.

Only free-text safety answer is structural oversight of the sheriff, plus rural mobile outreach for homelessness [S4]; nothing on enforcement or staffing, and the firearms 'yes' is off-axis. Low is honest.
'Yes' to local climate investments plus her own free-text line on climate action 'in partnership with the communities that are impacted the most' [S4]. One clear source, medium.

First council run; her only office is the Charter Review Commission seat [S3][S5]. In S4 she argues for 'diversity of representation' and for more people running 'to bring a new perspective' instead of 'the same names on the ballot year after year' (checked in the cached copy). Her statement's stress on collaboration and compromise as Charter Review chair [S10] keeps it at +1.
